pages.title: Axiom Fragment
pages.text: A shard of a foundational rule. Mathematics is built on axioms that cannot be proven but must be assumed, and reality appears to be built the same way. This fragment holds one of those rules, and when I hold it, I feel very sure of something I cannot name.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Law Wraiths in the hyperdimensional reality drop these when they dissolve. In the Axiom Distiller, I learned to boil down a Primordial Law into its foundational assumptions and crystallise them.
